title: Implement Promise.all
description: Reimplement Promise.all from scratch — wait for every input to resolve, preserve order, reject fast on the first error. Classic async interview question.

notes: Wrap each entry with `Promise.resolve()` — values may be raw, not promises, but you still want a microtask boundary.
Track completion with a counter, not by checking `out` for empty slots. A resolved `undefined` is still a real result.
Empty input must resolve to `[]` synchronously (well, in a microtask). Forgetting this gives a forever-pending promise.

questions.q: Why preallocate `out = new Array(arr.length)` instead of pushing as each resolves?
options: Promises may resolve out of order — assigning by index preserves input order
Push throws inside a Promise constructor

questions.q: What happens when one input rejects?
options: Other inputs are cancelled and the outer promise rejects
Other inputs keep running, but the outer promise rejects with the first error and ignores later results
It waits for all to settle, then collects errors
It silently resolves with undefined at that index
Items may be plain values; Promise.resolve normalizes them to thenables
It speeds up the event loop
It should reject — nothing to wait for

exercises.prompt: Fill in promiseAll so [Promise.resolve(1), 2, Promise.resolve(3)] logs [1,2,3].

blanks.hint: static Promise method that wraps a value
forward errors to the outer promise

L3.prompt: Implement promiseAll(arr) that resolves to an in-order array of resolved values, or rejects with the first error. Test with a mix of promises and bare values; also test the rejection path.
hints: Wrap each entry in Promise.resolve() so plain values become thenables.
Assign results by index; track completion with a counter.
Forward the first .catch directly to the outer reject — later errors are ignored.
